LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 6.3.1 PHRASAL QUANTIFIERS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we tell countable nouns from uncountable ones?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts
2. use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 6.3.1 PHRASAL QUANTIFIERS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 6.3.1 PHRASAL QUANTIFIERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers to a partner. (skill: use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts.
3. Practise this skill: use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we tell countable nouns from uncountable ones?
2. Which words are used to show the amount of something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Phrasal Quantifiers means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise phrasal quantifiers in oral and written contexts.
5. Be able to: use phrasal quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
